Fixture: 81_alpha_rgba_600x520_lossless.jxl
600x520 RGBA, modular lossless, 8-bit colour and 8-bit alpha

Purpose
-------
Wave 6 rung 2, and the multi-group rung AGENTS.md section 6 requires of any
path that can see more than one group. At group_dim 256 the frame is a 3x3
grid of groups, so every channel -- alpha included -- exceeds group_dim in
both directions and G.1.3 stops before it. The alpha samples then arrive in
the nine G.4.2 pass-group sub-bitstreams, one rectangle each, and a decoder
that got the per-group rectangle or the copy-back position wrong produces a
tiled or offset alpha channel rather than an error.

Frame structure, as parsed by JPXL itself (jpxl-decode's own frame-header
reader, not by any oracle):

  frame 0  kRegularFrame  kModular  9 groups (3x3), 1 LF group
           1 extra channel (kAlpha), ec_upsampling 1, dim_shift 0

The colour content is the shape the VarDCT and progressive recipes use -- a
smooth left half and a 1-pixel checkerboard right half, the highest spatial
frequency a discrete grid can represent, so cjxl's own transform-selection
heuristic reaches for a mixture of varblock sizes. This sidecar does not claim
particular transforms were chosen.

The alpha content is deliberately NOT the same shape as the colour: a radial
ramp with a hard-edged fully transparent notch in the top-left quadrant. A
decode that transposed the alpha plane with a colour plane, shifted it, or
dropped it and left zeros therefore cannot produce a plausible image, and the
test asserts the alpha plane is non-constant before it grades anything.

Grading (18181-3 4.2)
---------------------
Lossless, so the reference decode and ours agree exactly as integers; the only
tolerance the test allows is the f32 round-trip of those integers, at
peak <= 1e-6 and RMSE <= 1e-6. The alpha channel is additionally held to a
peak of 1e-6 on its own.

Grading is against a reference DECODE of this stream (the committed .npy, or a
fresh djxl decode), never against the original source PNG -- Part 3 conformance
bounds decoder-vs-reference error, not encoder loss against the pre-encode
image.

Provenance
----------

  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 0 -e 7
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-alpha-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_alpha_rgba_600x520.png  (536823 bytes)
                sha256 fa5dcf44f145d2487385b6e2025fcd800c2bc0662cf8f5264eec8cdcce0aebd8
                Synthetic PNG, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-alpha-fixtures.sh with nothing but the standard
                library -- no third-party image was used, converted or
                consulted, and no image library is involved. PNG rather than
                PNM because PNM has no alpha channel.

  Fixture:      34504 bytes
                sha256 786b70816031bd63b076e81b15cdbbe2413fb1c46725d5542f82533459c6e6f1

  Reference decode (djxl --output_format npy):
    81_alpha_rgba_600x520_lossless.npy  (4992080 bytes)
    sha256 4ccd38593ebdf01cc3a36b9c9de0948252dc336c417006ebff8e66b9b9e9bd22
    NOT committed (>= 100 KB); the test regenerates it with the pinned djxl,
    and skips if no djxl is present.
    Shape (1, 520, 600, 4) little-endian f32, per 18181-3 4.1.2. The channel count
    includes the alpha channel: djxl interleaves the extra channels after the
    colour ones, which is the same order G.1.3 gives the modular channel list
    and the order jpxl-decode returns its planes in. Readable with
    jpxl_conformance::FloatImage::from_npy.
    Regenerable at any time from the fixture with the pinned djxl build
    (decode is deterministic per libjxl revision, see PINNED_REVISIONS.txt).

cjxl/djxl are used strictly as BLACK BOXES: they emit/consume conformant
streams for JPXL to parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a
different libjxl revision changes these digests, that is the point of
recording them -- do not silently update them; note the revision change.
